style: Stylised historical cartography featuring muted parchment tones, flat-colour territorial fills, and minimalist cartoon character avatars. Dynamic pan-and-zoom camera movements across continental maps interspersed with comedic character expressions.
narration: Energetic, engaging educational explainer tone delivered at a brisk conversational pace.
never_change: Parchment-textured continental base map with bold territorial boundary fills.

facts.detail: American envoys travel to Europe aiming to purchase a single strategic port city.
Negotiators unexpectedly receive an offer to purchase the entire continental territory.
In 1802, two major European powers enter a brief truce despite looming hostility.
The French ruler retains grand imperial ambitions anchored by extensive North American holdings.
The cornerstone of French Caribbean wealth is Saint-Domingue, driven by sugar and coffee plantations.
Enslaved workers endure brutal forced labour to fuel this colony's massive agricultural output.
An organized revolt by the enslaved population strips France of colonial control.
Taking advantage of peace in Europe, French forces cross the Atlantic to recapture the island.
Tropical epidemic yellow fever decimates French troops, forcing complete abandonment.
Losing the Caribbean sugar colony renders the mainland territory strategically useless to Paris.
The western frontier of the young American republic relies heavily on river navigation for shipping.
Outbound trade funnels through the French-controlled river gateway of New Orleans.
In 1803, American leadership dispatches negotiators with a ten-million-dollar offer for New Orleans.
Impending conflict with the British leaves Paris in dire need of war funds and unable to defend distant land.
The French counter-offer tenders the entire territory for fifteen million dollars.
Despite lacking presidential authority for such a grand acquisition, the diplomats accept.
The land deal instantly doubles the nation's geographical size at approximately four cents per acre.
